FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: The fee half is right and the waiver half is missing, and the obligation is scored as one. FEE - correct: MO.memo.json rules.fees says 'Not fixed by Article XIV and county-variable ... No fee figure is published on this track', and filing-instructions.md publishes no figure: 'The held sources establish no filing fee for this petition and this packet states no amount. Ask the clerk.' That is the right answer for Missouri and this factory's own regression test (scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/test-md-pardon-record-disclosures.mjs) names that sentence as true here. WAIVER - absent: MO.memo.json rules.feeWaiver names a waiver route for this track by form number and authority - 'GN10 under Rule 77.03 and section 514.040 where the participant cannot pay and the filing court accepts the statewide form. Not generated by default on this route, because a large share of Article XIV participants have no filing to pay for.' The packet states that route NOWHERE. Measured by exhaustive case-insensitive search across every participant-facing byte this family delivers - participant-instructions.md, filing-instructions.md and the full pdftotext -layout extraction of canonical.pdf: zero occurrences of 'waiver', 'GN10', '514.040', '77.03', 'cannot pay', 'in forma pauperis' or 'indigen'. The word 'fee' appears twice in the whole delivered set, both in the two-line Fees section of filing-instructions.md. The record's stated reason bears on whether to GENERATE the form, not on whether to TELL the participant the route exists, and it concedes on its own face that some participants on this route do have a filing to pay for - which is exactly the population a waiver serves. A participant who cannot pay is told only to ask the clerk about an amount, and is never told Missouri has a statewide fee-waiver form or the rule that authorises it.

SERVICE.detail: MO.memo.json rules.service is 'None performed by the participant. CR375 carries no certificate of service', and rules.notice is 'Not prescribed for the participant ... the court and clerk handle notice as they do on the other petition routes. Article XIV prescribes no objection window and no prosecutorial notice period of its own.' The delivered packet matches on both limbs, verified on the page rather than in the report: the full text extraction of all 10 delivered pages contains no certificate of service, no certificate of mailing and no service block, and neither instruction file directs the participant to serve anyone. The three agencies named as Defendant(s) are named as record-holders whose records the order reaches, which is what the record says they are.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The memo declares 11 selfHelpStopConditions for this track. All 11 appear in participant-instructions.md VERBATIM, under a 'Stop conditions' heading that says in terms 'They are the conditions the Missouri record for this route states, in its own words' - I compared them string by string against MO.memo.json rather than reading the builder's claim, and this build refuses if the record stops declaring them (source-receipt.compositionSources pins MO.memo.json by sha, which I rehashed and it matches). Two further stops are added and correctly labelled as route boundaries rather than record conditions: a non-Missouri or non-marijuana conviction, and a still-pending charge. The packet also states where self-help ends inside the copy itself - 'If that is no longer true, stop: the other box applies to you, this packet is drafted for the wrong branch'.

Statutory source note: Acts 2023, No. 342, Sec. 1.'; page 4 line 3 'Assigned component identity: la-977d-marijuana-first-offense-proposed-order-2'; page 5 line 3 'Assigned component identity: la-977d-marijuana-first-offense-proposed-order-3'. This is the defect VF02 failed ri_multiple_misdemeanors-set on at this same base - a route's internal identifier printed on the filing. (2) Build-record analysis is printed five times on the filings, in the record's own internal vocabulary: page 1, 'The committed manual-completion record classifies both as manual completion items pending a data-protection review'; page 2, 'which the committed record makes the first condition on which self-help stops'; page 2, 'reproduced from the Article 998 statutory text this packet is bound to by content digest, as Article 986(A) requires'; page 3, 'The committed record requires both signature blocks the statute prints to be carried, which is why this one appears at all.' Those three are required participant inputs on the committed record, so they are carried here instead, on the order that identifies the record of arrest and conviction the decree reaches, rather than added to the face of a mandatory form.' That paragraph is addressed to this packet's own builder and reviewer and to nobody in the case. The record's own words belong in the guide, labelled as internal record text.' On this packet the guide, pages 7-19, is the right place and already does this well; the four filing pages are not.

COMPONENT_SET.detail: Five components declared; four generated and all four present in the delivered 19 pages in the manifested order. The fifth is the conditional Article 988 fee-exemption component and it is withheld. THE QUESTION THE BRIEF PUT WAS WHETHER THE PACKET AND ITS INSTRUCTIONS AGREE ABOUT WHAT IS ENCLOSED, AND MEASURED PAGE BY PAGE THEY DO. The record's item 4 sentence 'The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in' appears three times in the delivered canonical bytes, on pages 9, 12 and 14. Its correction, 'This packet does not give you the Article 988 form...', appears three times, on pages 9, 12 and 14 - the SAME PAGE as each claim, every time, immediately beneath it, and each correction states the condition the record gives, states that a conviction track does not meet it, states that no Article 988 form is enclosed, and then preserves the part of the item that still applies by telling the participant where to get the form and what filing without it costs. Page 9 also states the convention before the list begins: 'Where an item describes a document this packet does not contain, or names a form this track does not use, the record's words are printed unchanged and a correction is added beneath them.' I checked the page split deliberately, because a correction on the following page would leave a participant reading page N with a false statement; there is no such instance in either fixture. The withholding itself is defensible on the record's own condition (Article 983(F) grounds are non-conviction grounds; Article 977(D) is a conviction track) and the sibling family that generates it is on a different track, which the packet says.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.detail: All 25 declared values are on the delivered pages of both fixtures - I found 25 of 25 by string search rather than accepting the report. THE FAILURE IS THAT THE MOVER'S NAME IS WRITTEN IN THE INVERSE OF THE ORDER THE FORM'S OWN PRINTED CAPTION DEMANDS, ON A MANDATORY STATUTORY FORM, ON BOTH FIXTURES, AND NOTHING TELLS THE PARTICIPANT TO CORRECT IT. The Article 998 statutory text this packet is bound to prints 'NAME: ____ (Last, First, MI)' - I read that from the pinned source bytes. The delivered page 1 prints 'NAME (Last, First, MI): Jordan Avery Reyes' on canonical and 'NAME (Last, First, MI): Maria-Alejandra O'Shaughnessy-Whitfield' on boundary. The factory's own fixture personas are first Jordan / middle Avery / last Reyes and last O'Shaughnessy-Whitfield / first Maria-Alejandra, which I confirmed from the shared persona used across build scripts. So Part I of a motion filed with the clerk, and matched by the Bureau against the state rap sheet, states the mover's surname as 'Jordan'. This is the same defect VF07 recorded today on rcap-hi-custom-pleading, where the caption was 'Current Legal Name (Last, First, Middle):' and the ink was given-name-first. Searched both instruction documents and all 19 delivered pages: no sentence anywhere tells the participant the name order, and the packet's own guide insists on rap-sheet matching for race and gender ('written as the state rap sheet writes it, so Part I matches the record the Bureau holds') while saying nothing about the name. TWO FURTHER FIDELITY ITEMS ON THE SAME MANDATORY FORM, RECORDED WITH IT because they share a repair. (a) The family asserts twice - build-findings 'no field the statutory form does not print was added to it' and packet-set-manifest.fieldsDeliberatelyNotAddedToThisForm - that Article 986(C) was applied without exception, and the delivered Article 998 motion prints three fields the statute does not: 'Whether the conviction is a misdemeanour or a felony: Misdemeanour' (a WRITE, LA-CCRP-ART-998.conviction_level, in the family's own actual-writes), 'Statute the mover was convicted under' and 'Whether this was the mover's first offense for possession of marijuana, tetrahydrocannabinol or a chemical derivative'. I read the pinned statutory source end to end: its Part II is the heading and 'l. Mover was convicted on ___/___/___ (MM/DD/YYYY)' and then the prayer, and it prints none of those three. The build applied its own 986(C) rule to the arrest date, the count and the original charges and moved them to the Article 992 order, then added three others to the same page. (b) The statute prints '(MM/DD/YYYY)' beside both of its date lines; the delivered motion drops that instruction and writes ISO - 'DOB: 1991-04-17' and '1. Mover was convicted on 2026-02-11' - on the form whose date the ninety-day computation runs from.

All 15 required-before-filing items are reproduced verbatim and numbered ('Item n of 15') in the delivered guide, with the count printed beside the list so short carriage would be visible on the page. Three lines of the controlling record name a sibling's form - I confirmed all three in LA.memo.json: rules.participantSignature, the required-before-filing item and the sign action all read 'The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed If not represented by counsel'. All three appear in the delivered bytes verbatim, on pages 10, 13 and 15, and all three carry the correction on THE SAME PAGE, immediately beneath: 'There is no Article 989 Motion in this packet, and none is used on this track... Read the item as referring to the Article 998 Motion enclosed with this packet, and sign THAT one in its block headed "If not represented by counsel".' The correction is actionable because the thing it points at exists and I found it: the delivered Article 998 motion on canonical page 3 prints the block headed 'IF NOT REPRESENTED BY COUNSEL - UNREPRESENTED MOVER BLOCK' with an empty signature line and an empty date line. The correction also cites the same record's own contradicting line, rules.filing, which says in terms that 'the Article 989 form is not used here' - which I read in LA.memo.json and which is reproduced verbatim in the delivered pages. A participant following this packet signs the right document. Every one of the 15 items' disclosure text and every participantMustSupply string reaches the delivered pages; the first requiredBeforeFiling item, the FIRST-OFFENCE averment that is the whole eligibility test, is left blank on the motion AND on the Article 992 order, disclosed in the supply table, and named again as the first self-help stop condition.
